wv_creekside_boulder.blurb: A single freestanding sandstone boulder in the Deer Skull group above Cheat Canyon, a short walk into the woods from its parking area. It is climbed on all four sides, so the twelve problems are unusually varied: a dihedral running into an overhanging prow on the highway side, slab on two faces, and a vertical featured wall opposite. Grades run from the very easiest up to V8, with most problems in the V0 to V1 range and a few stiffer lines above V4, so a mixed group can all find something. Bring a pad or two and scout the walk-off before you top out.

wv_fat_rat_boulders.blurb: A small scatter of sandstone boulders on the Furnace Road side of Coopers Rock State Forest, near the road and a camp spot. It is a low-key stop rather than a place to plan a day around, but it holds a dozen problems with a wide spread: a handful of easy lines from the very easiest up to V3, a middle group around V4 to V6, and one far harder project. Good for a quick session when you are already working the nearby Furnace Road boulders. The rock is coarse sandstone that dries slowly after rain, so avoid it wet.
wv_fat_rat_boulders.approach: Drive down the forest's Furnace Road past the roof-rocks pull-off to a campsite marker on the left, park there, and follow the path toward the campsite. The first boulder downhill and slightly right begins the cluster.

wv_grunge_boulder_the.blurb: One proud, tall sandstone boulder among the Furnace Trail boulders at Coopers Rock State Forest, reached by a trail down the hillside from the Iron Furnace trailhead lot. A steep overhanging face leads to high topouts, and rocks sit in some landings, so bring several pads and a spotter. The dozen problems skew hard for the forest: a few V2 to V5 lines, then a solid block of V6 to V7, and several problems from V8 into the V10 range. Not the place for a warm-up, but a strong session for people climbing around V6 and up.

wv_warm_up_boulders.blurb: A friendly group of boulders in the Roadside section of Coopers Rock State Forest, within the First Set cluster. Eleven problems on sandstone, and the bulk are very easy: most sit at V0, a few at V1 and V2, with a single harder corner line near V4. That makes it a natural first stop for beginners or anyone loosening up before moving on to the steeper blocks nearby. As elsewhere in the forest, let the coarse rock dry fully after rain before pulling on.

wv_forgotten_block_area_the_climbs.blurb: A cluster of sandstone blocks in the Upper Rock City section of Coopers Rock State Forest, the zone at the far end of the park road. Almost everything here is bouldering, ten problems from V2 to V7 with the bulk in the middle of that range, plus one short trad line at a hard grade. Upper Rock City is busier than some of the forest's other main bouldering zones, so expect company on weekends. The rock is coarse, grippy sandstone; leave it to dry after rain before pulling on.

wv_i_love_luci_boulder.blurb: A roofed sandstone boulder at Meadow Top in the Meadow River Gorge, part of the New River Gorge region. The eleven problems cover a broad range: a good number of V0 and V1 lines to start on, a few V2 to V3, and then a small set of much harder problems reaching V9. The large roof is the boulder's signature, and Meadow Top in general is well shaded in summer, which helps through the warm months.
